C005.subject: Large language models with self-play and recursive self-improvement
C005.predicate: will demonstrate a phase transition in general reasoning capability at a critical parameter scale, which
C005.object: reduces the timeline to AGI to under 10 years
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Large language models with self-play and recursive self-improvement reduces the timeline to AGI to under 10 years]

[PATH:empirical] Systematic scaling experiments on LLMs with self-play fine-tuning (e.g., AlphaGo-style iterative improvement) across multiple orders of magnitude in parameters, measuring reasoning benchmarks (e.g., MATH, ARC, MMLU) for discontinuous jumps. — Directly tests the phase transition claim by examining whether self-play and scale produce a sharp, nonlinear improvement in general reasoning, and whether that improvement accelerates the path to AGI.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of critical scaling laws in transformers with recursive self-improvement, using frameworks like statistical mechanics of learning or neural scaling laws to predict when reasoning capabilities might undergo a phase transition. — Provides a formal basis for understanding whether a phase transition is mathematically plausible at a given parameter scale, and under what conditions it could shorten the timeline to AGI.

[PATH:literature] Literature review of historical self-play systems (e.g., AlphaZero, MuZero) and their generalization to non-game domains, combined with meta-analyses of emergent abilities in LLMs (e.g., Wei et al. 2022, Schaeffer et al. 2023). — Contextualizes the hypothesis by examining whether self-play-driven emergent reasoning has been observed in other domains and whether such emergence typically leads to rapid AGI timelines, offering comparative evidence to confirm or refute the claim.

scope.domain: machine learning scaling and emergent capabilities

C006.subject: Current limitations of large language models
C006.object: AGI is unlikely to be achieved within 20 years
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Current limitations of large language models AGI is unlikely to be achieved within 20 years]

[PATH:empirical] Systematic evaluation of LLMs on novel reasoning benchmarks (e.g., ARC-AGI, Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) over the next 5 years — If LLMs consistently fail to generalize to unseen abstract tasks despite scaling, this would support the hypothesis that current limitations are fundamental and AGI remains distant. Conversely, rapid improvement would refute it.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of computational and architectural constraints in transformer-based models (e.g., limitations of autoregressive generation, lack of causal world models) — A formal proof or strong argument that LLMs cannot achieve key AGI capabilities (e.g., true causal reasoning, long-term planning) would confirm the hypothesis. A demonstration of viable extensions (e.g., hybrid neuro-symbolic systems) would refute it.

[PATH:literature] Longitudinal literature review of AGI timelines and expert surveys (e.g., AI Impacts, Metaculus) updated with recent LLM breakthroughs — Tracking shifts in expert consensus and empirical evidence over the next decade can confirm or refute the 20-year timeline by identifying whether LLM limitations are being overcome or persist.

C007.subject: Hybrid neuro-symbolic cognitive architectures
C007.object: fundamental obstacles in reasoning and generalization within 10 years
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Hybrid neuro-symbolic cognitive architectures fundamental obstacles in reasoning and generalization within 10 years]

[PATH:empirical] Benchmarking on compositional generalization tasks (e.g., SCAN, COGS, or MathQA) comparing hybrid neuro-symbolic models against pure neural baselines over a 5-year longitudinal study — Direct empirical measurement of whether hybrid architectures achieve systematic generalization beyond statistical pattern matching, providing concrete evidence for overcoming a fundamental obstacle.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of expressiveness and sample complexity bounds for hybrid architectures (e.g., using results from logical neural networks, differentiable programming, or neural theorem provers) — Rigorous theoretical work can delineate the conditions under which hybrid models provably surpass the limitations of purely neural systems in reasoning tasks, confirming or refuting the feasibility of the 10-year timeline.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of recent progress in neuro-symbolic systems, including systematic reviews from venues like NeurIPS, ICLR, or AAAI, focusing on reported breakthroughs in out-of-distribution reasoning and transfer learning — A comprehensive literature review can assess the current trajectory and rate of progress, identifying whether the field is on pace to resolve key obstacles within the specified timeframe.

qualifier.tension: By integrating explicit symbolic reasoning with neural learning, hybrid architectures bypass the pure statistical limitations that prolong the timeline for current models.

C008.subject: Advances in cognitive architectures
C008.object: fundamental obstacles in reasoning and generalization within 10 years
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Advances in cognitive architectures fundamental obstacles in reasoning and generalization within 10 years]

[PATH:empirical] Longitudinal benchmark performance on the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC) by state-of-the-art cognitive architectures (e.g., architectures based on differentiable neural computers, hybrid neuro-symbolic systems) measured annually from 2025 to 2035 — ARC is specifically designed to test reasoning and generalization beyond pattern matching; consistent improvement to near-human or super-human levels would confirm the hypothesis, while stagnation or marginal gains would refute it.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of computational complexity bounds for general-purpose reasoning in cognitive architectures, specifically examining whether current neural and symbolic approaches can overcome the 'no-free-lunch' constraints for inductive generalization — If formal proofs show that fundamental obstacles (e.g., combinatorial explosion, requirement for task-specific priors) are inherent to any architecture within practical resource limits, the hypothesis is refuted; conversely, identification of novel algorithms that bypass these limits supports the hypothesis.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of published results from major cognitive architecture projects (e.g., SOAR, ACT-R, Nengo, and recent deep learning extensions) on tasks requiring systematic compositionality and out-of-distribution generalization, including systematic replication studies — A comprehensive review can reveal whether the field is on a trajectory to solve these obstacles within a decade, or whether progress has plateaued, providing evidence for or against the hypothesis.

C011.subject: Embodiment and sensorimotor integration
C011.predicate: are not necessary for AGI and
C011.object: a purely sensory-grounded language model with no physical body can achieve general intelligence within 15 years
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Embodiment and sensorimotor integration a purely sensory-grounded language model with no physical body can achieve general intelligence within 15 years]

[PATH:empirical] Compare performance of large language models (e.g., GPT-4, Gemini) on embodied reasoning benchmarks (e.g., ALFRED, EmbodiedQA, VirtualHome) against human or robot-in-the-loop baselines, focusing on tasks requiring physical causality, object manipulation, or spatial navigation. — If a purely sensory-grounded language model can match or exceed embodied agents on such benchmarks, it would support the hypothesis that embodiment is not necessary. Persistent failure on tasks requiring physical interaction would refute it.

[PATH:theoretical] Review and meta-analyze literature on the role of sensorimotor experience in cognitive development (e.g., Piagetian stages, 'grounded cognition' theory, and robotics studies like the 'tower-building' experiments by Brooks and colleagues). — This literature provides the foundational argument for why embodiment might be necessary. Demonstrating that key cognitive capacities (e.g., object permanence, causal inference) can be learned from purely sensory-linguistic data would challenge that foundation, while failure to replicate such learning would confirm the necessity.

[PATH:empirical] Conduct a controlled experiment training a transformer-based model on a massive multimodal dataset (text + images/video of physical interactions) but without any robotic embodiment or proprioceptive feedback, and test for generalization to novel physical tasks (e.g., predicting outcomes of unseen tool-use scenarios). — This directly tests the core claim: whether sensory grounding alone (without a body) suffices for general intelligence. Positive results would confirm the hypothesis; negative results (e.g., inability to generalize to novel physical dynamics) would refute it by showing persistent epistemic friction.

qualifier.tension: This hypothesis directly contradicts the original claim by asserting that embodiment is not a necessary condition for AGI, and that scaling sensory-language models alone can overcome the epistemic friction.

[PATH:empirical] Longitudinal benchmarking of deep reinforcement learning models on sensorimotor integration tasks (e.g., robotic manipulation, active perception) using standardized platforms like MuJoCo or real-world robot testbeds — Directly tests whether computational advances (e.g., transformer-based policies, world models) improve closed-loop sensorimotor performance over time, providing quantitative evidence for or against the predicted breakthrough within a decade.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of publication trends in interdisciplinary sensorimotor research (e.g., combining neuroscience, cognitive science, robotics, and AI) over the past 5 years, with projection models — Evaluates whether the rate of cross-disciplinary collaboration and methodological convergence is accelerating sufficiently to yield breakthroughs within the 10-year window, clarifying the plausibility of the hypothesis.
